name: AT&T Home Phone
why: Largest legacy Bell landline provider (22 states); national brand with its own myAT&T billing.

name: Verizon Home Phone (copper and Fios Digital Voice)
why: Major Northeast/Mid-Atlantic landline provider; national brand with My Verizon billing.

name: CenturyLink (Lumen) Home Phone
why: One of the largest ILEC landline footprints (former Qwest/Embarq territory).

name: Frontier Communications
why: Large national ILEC landline provider (25 states) with its own billing site.

name: Kinetic by Windstream
why: Large rural/suburban ILEC (18 states); distinct Go Kinetic billing site.

name: Brightspeed
why: Former CenturyLink ILEC territory (20 states) now a separate landline provider with its own billing.

name: Consolidated Communications (Fidium)
why: Multi-state ILEC (18 states, incl. legacy FairPoint in northern New England); replaces the Cox roster record (a CA Lifeline CLEC entity, not Cox's billing site).

name: TDS Telecom
why: Large rural ILEC group (27 states) with its own TDS ePay billing; replaces the Spectrum roster record (a FL Lifeline CLEC entity; Spectrum's real billing site is already covered by another category's dossier).

name: altafiber (Cincinnati Bell)
why: Legacy Bell ILEC for Greater Cincinnati with its own My altafiber billing; replaces Ooma, whose official public pages document almost no billing behaviour (card-on-file only, no bill).

name: Vonage Home Phone
why: Long-standing national VoIP home phone brand with its own account billing (card on file, paperless only).
